name: Bar Chart
when_to_pick: Compare one numeric metric across 2-8 discrete categories, ideally with two series side-by-side per category so the gap between them is the story (e.g., backtest vs. live win rate per strategy, p50 vs. p99 latency per broker type, or expected vs. realized return per asset). Reach for chart_area instead when the x-axis is time or a continuous progression; use chart_stacked_bar when the series sum to a whole.

title.description: Chart title rendered above the plot. State the metric and unit, e.g. 'Backtest vs. live win rate by strategy (%)'.

caption.description: One-sentence takeaway shown below the chart. Name the insight a reader would miss from the bars alone (the largest gap, the outlier, the trend) rather than restating the axis.

labels.description: Category names on the x-axis, one per group of bars. Keep them short (1-3 words) so they don't wrap.

datasets.description: One entry per series. Two contrasting series (e.g. expected vs. actual) usually read strongest; cap at 4 so bars stay legible.

label.description: Series name shown in the legend, e.g. 'Backtest' or 'Live (90 days)'.

data.description: One value per label, in the same order as labels. Length must equal labels.length.

tone.description: Semantic fill color. Use 'success'/'danger' only for genuinely good/bad series (BUY/SELL, profit/loss); use 'accent'/'neutral' for non-directional categories.
